logicalBugs.description: A Gitea pull request proposes a code change and summarizes the commits to be merged. When it contains exactly one commit, that summary says “1 commits,” using the plural form for a single commit.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The pull title summary translation interpolates a count into a fixed commits string instead of selecting singular/plural wording.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea pull request proposes a code change and summarizes the commits to be merged. When it contains exactly one commit, that summary says “1 commits,” using the plural form for a single commit.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea pull request (a proposed code change), open Files Changed for the latest single commit and submit text from its enabled Review panel. No review is posted: a technical error appears, the page remains on the commit-specific view, and the draft stays in the panel instead of completing the offered review.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The latest-commit diff qualifies as IsShowingAllCommits, enabling the review form. That form appends /reviews/submit to .Link, which on the commit view includes /commits/<sha>; only the PR-scoped review route exists.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea pull request’s latest single-commit Files Changed view, open the enabled Review panel and submit a comment. The submission fails at a nonexistent commit-specific endpoint and posts no review, rather than completing the offered review action.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and pull request (a proposed code change) form actions can expose a raw JSON-parsing SyntaxError labelled Network error when the server rejects an unavailable or unauthorized action. Confirmed triggers include stale deleted/locked/archived comment or issue (a tracked work item) forms, deleted milestone (a named group of work items)/time-entry targets and rejected review actions; the UI does not explain the actual refusal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a failed Review-panel submission receives a plaintext HTTP 404, but the UI labels a resulting client JSON parse exception as a network error.

In Gitea, after an author submits a comment-only review of their own pull request, the reviewer sidebar offers Re-request review for that author. The action fails with a raw network/JSON exception on every attempt.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, reviewed by you on global or organization Pull Requests omits a pull request (a proposed code change) that the signed-in user both authored and submitted a persisted Comment review on. The omission occurs without a keyword search, distinguishing it from stale search-index review data.
logicalBugs.rootCause: applyReviewedCondition intersects review/comment membership with issue.poster_id <> viewer. Accepted comment-only self reviews therefore cannot satisfy the filter, on global and organization dashboards.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Pull Requests dashboard, choose Reviewed by you after submitting a persisted Comment review on a pull request you also authored. The filter still shows no matching pull request, including after refresh, even without a text-search keyword.

On a Gitea organization's Pull Requests page, 'Reviewed by you' doesn't list a pull request the user authored and submitted a Comment review on, because the filter excludes the user's own pull requests.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, global/organization dashboards can list and count issues (tracked work items) or pull requests (proposed code changes) from a repository whose corresponding unit is disabled, and organization/team issue dashboards can include issues for a Code-only team without Issues access. The title remains actionable but opens 404 even though the repository itself may be readable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SearchRepositoryCondition admits owned organization repositories and checks actor access with unit.TypeInvalid. The Issues UnitType does not constrain those repositories; dashboard search then loads their issues without per-issue unit authorization. Both disabled trackers and teams with Issues No Access pass this same repository selection.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after Pull Requests is disabled for a repository, the global dashboard still includes its open pull request in results and counts, presenting an unavailable pull request as actionable.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, combining a matching keyword with Assigned to you or an Assignee filter can hide correctly assigned issues (tracked work items) and pull requests (proposed code changes) on repository, global and organization lists. Explicit user and Assigned to anybody filters are affected; either the keyword alone or the assignment-filtered list without a keyword can still find the same record.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Indexer conversion copies Issue.AssigneeID, a nonpersisted legacy field, instead of Issue.Assignees. Specific, self and any-assignee filters therefore query incorrect indexed data. Non-keyword database filtering uses issue_assignees and succeeds.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s global Pull Requests dashboard lists an assigned pull request without a query, but searching a matching title term under Assigned to you hides it while the same query under Created by you finds it.

On a Gitea organization's Pull Requests page, 'Assigned to you' with a text search shows No results even though a pull request assigned to the user matches it. The search index doesn't store current assignees.

On a Gitea repository’s Pull Requests list, combine a matching keyword with Assigned to you or an explicit Assignee. A pull request with that saved assignment disappears even though the keyword alone and the assignment filter without a keyword can find it.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, bulk Open can reopen a pull request that the pull request detail page refuses to reopen, including when its head branch is deleted or an identical pull request is already open. The bulk/API path leaves an invalid open pull request or duplicate open pull requests (proposed code changes) instead of enforcing the detail page’s refusal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The bulk issue status handler invokes ReopenIssue directly. It omits the detail-page checks for an existing identical open PR and a usable source branch, allowing invalid duplicate or broken reopen states.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, bulk Open reopens a closed pull request after its head branch is deleted, bypassing the detail page’s explicit reopening prohibition and leaving a broken open pull request.

In Gitea, reopening a closed pull request from its own page is refused while an identical pull request is open, but selecting it in the Closed list and choosing bulk Open reopens it anyway, leaving two identical open pull requests.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on global or organization Issues and Pull Requests, submitting a text search clears the selected Author or Assignee. The search results then include matching records by other authors or assigned to other users/nobody, even though the user intended to narrow the existing filtered list.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared dashboard search form submits only type, sort, state and search-combo fields. It has no poster or assignee hidden input, so submitting a keyword discards those filters on both global and organization dashboards.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, submitting text search on the global pull request dashboard drops its selected Author filter and admits pull requests by other authors.
In Gitea, submitting search on the top-level Pull Requests dashboard drops the selected assignee filter and displays a matching unassigned pull request that was excluded before the search.

On a Gitea organization's Pull Requests page, submitting a text search after choosing an Author removes the Author filter, so pull requests by other authors appear. The search form doesn't carry the poster value.

On a Gitea organization's Pull Requests page, submitting a text search after choosing an Assignee removes the Assignee filter, so pull requests assigned to someone else appear. The search form doesn't carry the assignee value.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea pull request (a proposed code change) discussion, Quote Reply places a source comment’s quoted text in the reply composer. Submitting that reply produces a saved comment without the quoted text, and reloading does not recover it. This concerns content lost during posting, separately from the case where Quote Reply leaves Comment disabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The report observes saved content loss, distinct from the confirmed stale Comment-button state. The pinned quote handler assigns the ComboMarkdownEditor value and the submission form reads its textarea; the exact event/editor synchronization sequence that loses the quote has not been established from source. Keep this attribution separate until the submitted form payload and active editor mode are known. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea pull request discussion, Quote Reply places a source comment’s quoted text in the reply composer. Submitting that reply produces a saved comment without the quoted text, and reloading does not recover it. This concerns content lost during posting, separately from the case where Quote Reply leaves Comment disabled.

logicalBugs.description: On Gitea’s global Issues or Pull Requests dashboard, choosing an explicit Author or Assignee does not give the filter control a visible active state distinct from no filter. The URL/results may be filtered correctly, but the closed controls do not reveal that restriction.
logicalBugs.rootCause: filter_item_user_fetch records the selected username only in a data attribute used inside the remote dropdown. The closed control always renders the same title and classes, regardless of selection.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Pull Requests dashboard, select a named user in the Assignee filter and close the menu. The control still shows only the generic Assignee label with no active-state indication, so the visible controls do not reveal the applied restriction.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s repository setting Ignore Whitespace for Conflicts saves and reloads as enabled, but conflict detection never uses it by default, so a pull request (a proposed code change) whose only difference from the base is whitespace is still marked conflicting and cannot be merged.
logicalBugs.rootCause: checkConflicts first attempts a three-way merge without the setting. If it conflicts and TestConflictingPatchesWithGitApply is disabled, it returns Conflict immediately. IgnoreWhitespaceConflicts is consulted only later for git apply --ignore-whitespace, so the default path never uses it.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s repository setting Ignore Whitespace for Conflicts saves and reloads as enabled, but conflict detection never uses it by default, so a pull request whose only difference from the base is whitespace is still marked conflicting and cannot be merged.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, submitting a review with text (Comment, Approve or Request changes) saves it and shows it in the timeline, but the pull request's Conversation tab count and the pull request (a proposed code change) list's comment count don't increase. Reloading doesn't fix them; the count is corrected only when an ordinary comment is later posted.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Review submission creates/updates CommentTypeReview outside the ordinary comment recount path. NumComments remains stale until an ordinary comment triggers UpdateIssueNumComments, which includes review comments in its aggregate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, submitting a review with text (Comment, Approve or Request changes) saves it and shows it in the timeline, but the pull request's Conversation tab count and the pull request list's comment count don't increase. Reloading doesn't fix them; the count is corrected only when an ordinary comment is later posted.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, with Enable autodetect manual merge turned on in repository settings, a pull request's View command line instructions still warn that the merge cannot be detected because autodetect manual merge is not enabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The instruction template checks the page-root .AutodetectManualMerge rather than the PullRequestsConfig value. The PR view does not set that root field, so it renders the disabled warning even when the repository option is on.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with Enable autodetect manual merge turned on in repository settings, a pull request's View command line instructions still warn that the merge cannot be detected because autodetect manual merge is not enabled.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, opening Files Changed on an empty pull request can return a bare HTTP 400 page instead of an empty diff. This affects initially equal branches and pull requests (proposed code changes) made empty by a successful rebase update, while their conversation page can remain available.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The diff handler requires afterCommitID to occur in prInfo.Commits. For an equal-branches or rebase-emptied PR the list is empty; the handler returns bare HTTP 400 before rendering the page instead of an empty diff.
reproductionPaths: Gitea allows creating a pull request between equal branches ('This pull request will be empty'), but opening that pull request's Files Changed tab replaces the whole page with a bare HTTP 400 error, 'after commit not found in pull request commits', with no navigation.

In Gitea, when Update branch by rebase succeeds but leaves the pull request with zero commits of its own (its changes are already in the base), opening Files Changed replaces the whole page with the plain text 'after commit not found in pull request commits' instead of showing the pull request with an empty diff.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after inline editing and saving an issue (a tracked work item) body or pull request (a proposed code change) description, newly rendered Markdown task-list checkboxes no longer respond or persist clicks. Reloading the page restores working checkboxes for that same saved text.
logicalBugs.rootCause: saveAndRefresh replaces renderContent.innerHTML but only attaches reference popups; it never calls initMarkupTasklist on the replacement markup. Page initialization attaches those handlers after reload.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after editing and saving a pull request description that contains a task list, the rendered task checkboxes are disabled and cannot be toggled until the page is reloaded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a closed pull request (a proposed code change), the title editor still lets the user pick a different 'merge into' branch, but Save fails with the toast 'Failed to update pull request target branch:' and nothing after the colon, and the editor stays open.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared title editor throws an error using resp.statusText without reading the JSON error/user_error payload. HTTP/2 statusText may be empty, so a valid closed-PR HTTP 409 becomes an empty-reason toast.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a closed pull request, the title editor still lets the user pick a different 'merge into' branch, but Save fails with the toast 'Failed to update pull request target branch:' and nothing after the colon, and the editor stays open.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after Cancel in an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) title editor, reopening it reuses the discarded title or target-branch selection. On a pull request, saving a later title edit can therefore also apply the previously cancelled target-branch change.
logicalBugs.rootCause: initRepoIssueTitleEdit uses one Cancel handler for the title and pull-target controls. It only hides the shared editor; it never resets the title value or #pull-target-branch data-branch to the saved values. Reopening/submitting reuses those stale controls.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea pull request's title editor, choosing a different 'merge into' branch and clicking Cancel doesn't discard that choice. The change stays pending in the editor and is applied the next time the editor is saved, even for a title-only edit.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on a draft pull request (a proposed code change) whose title is only a WIP prefix ('WIP:', '[WIP]' or 'wip:'), clicking 'Remove WIP: prefix' reloads the page with no change and no message; the pull request stays a draft and can't be merged.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The WIP action posts the stripped title, which is empty when the title contains only a prefix. UpdateIssueTitle returns no content without updating, while the action treats any successful HTTP status as success and reloads.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on a draft pull request whose title is only a WIP prefix ('WIP:', '[WIP]' or 'wip:'), clicking 'Remove WIP: prefix' reloads the page with no change and no message; the pull request stays a draft and can't be merged.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if the base branch gains a new commit while a 'Fast-forward only' merge confirmation is open, confirming it shows 'server error: 500' instead of explaining that the base changed. The pull request (a proposed code change) correctly stays unmerged.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The merge form allows a style based on previously computed CommitsBehind. A newly advanced base makes the actual ff-only merge fail, but the merge error path does not translate that stale-base condition to a readable conflict response.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if the base branch gains a new commit while a 'Fast-forward only' merge confirmation is open, confirming it shows 'server error: 500' instead of explaining that the base changed. The pull request correctly stays unmerged.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a pull request's conversation is locked, users without write access (including the pull request's own author when not a collaborator) can no longer post general comments, but can still post inline code comments, submit reviews (Comment, Approve, Request changes) and reply to review threads.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateCodeComment and SubmitReview check ordinary PR permissions/review validity but omit the IsLocked/nonwriter check used by ordinary CreateComment. Locking therefore blocks only the general discussion path.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a pull request's conversation is locked, users without write access (including the pull request's own author when not a collaborator) can no longer post general comments, but can still post inline code comments, submit reviews (Comment, Approve, Request changes) and reply to review threads.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when Manually merged is the only merge style enabled in repository settings, an open, mergeable pull request (a proposed code change) says 'This pull request cannot be merged because all repository merge options are disabled' and offers no Manually merged control. Enabling any automatic style makes Manually merged appear in the merge dropdown.
logicalBugs.rootCause: pull_merge_box renders the general merge style selector only if an automatic style is enabled. AllowManualMerge appears inside the selector but is omitted from its enclosing OR condition.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when Manually merged is the only merge style enabled in repository settings, an open, mergeable pull request says 'This pull request cannot be merged because all repository merge options are disabled' and offers no Manually merged control. Enabling any automatic style makes Manually merged appear in the merge dropdown.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea pull request (a proposed code change) can be marked Manually merged after its changes were merged outside the web interface. Checking Delete Branch in that confirmation, including when it is preselected by repository settings, records the merge but leaves the source branch undeleted instead of honoring the checked option.
logicalBugs.rootCause: MergePullRequest handles manuallyMerged and returns after MergedManually and redirect. The DeleteBranchAfterMerge cleanup is only reached by the later ordinary merge path.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea pull request can be marked Manually merged after its changes were merged outside the web interface. Checking Delete Branch in that confirmation, including when it is preselected by repository settings, records the merge but leaves the source branch undeleted instead of honoring the checked option.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after closing and reopening a draft (WIP) pull request (a proposed code change), the merge box first shows the 'Remove WIP: prefix' button, then about two seconds later its automatic refresh redraws the box without it. Reloading the page brings the button back.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The full PR page sets IsIssuePoster; the separately rendered merge_box response does not provide the same page context. Replacing the box after reopen removes author-only controls until full-page navigation restores that field.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after closing and reopening a draft (WIP) pull request, the merge box first shows the 'Remove WIP: prefix' button, then about two seconds later its automatic refresh redraws the box without it. Reloading the page brings the button back.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a pull request's branch is updated by rebase (or force-pushed), the Conversation timeline says the user 'added 2 commits' and lists both the old and the rewritten commit, although the pull request (a proposed code change) now contains one commit. The force-push isn't recorded on the stored push event, so it is rendered as an ordinary push.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreatePushPullComment carries IsForcePush on CreateCommentOptions and chooses old/new IDs accordingly, but comment persistence does not transfer that flag into the Comment record. The renderer consequently labels the two IDs as added commits.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a pull request's branch is updated by rebase (or force-pushed), the Conversation timeline says the user 'added 2 commits' and lists both the old and the rewritten commit, although the pull request now contains one commit. The force-push isn't recorded on the stored push event, so it is rendered as an ordinary push.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, reopening a closed pull request (a proposed code change) whose source branch is in a different repository (for example from a fork) fails with 'The origin branch is delete, cannot reopen.' even though the source branch still exists. The check looks for the target branch's name in the source repository, so it only passes if the source repository happens to have a branch with that name.
logicalBugs.rootCause: CreateComment’s reopen path checks IsBranchExist(pull.HeadRepo,pull.BaseBranch). It should check the source HeadBranch in that repository; a fork without the target branch name is incorrectly treated as having a deleted source.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, reopening a closed pull request whose source branch is in a different repository (for example from a fork) fails with 'The origin branch is delete, cannot reopen.' even though the source branch still exists. The check looks for the target branch's name in the source repository, so it only passes if the source repository happens to have a branch with that name.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when 'Update branch by rebase' can't rebase a pull request's branch (for example because earlier commits conflict when replayed, even though the current files were reconciled), the page simply reloads: the branch is still out of date, its commits are unchanged, and nothing explains why the update didn't happen. The defect is the missing failure feedback, not that the rebase failed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The pinned UpdatePullRequest handler explicitly flashes merge/rebase conflicts and generic errors before redirecting. The report’s missing feedback cannot be explained as a missing error branch in this handler. The error propagation or redirected flash rendering path needs further evidence. The exact cause remains unresolved.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when 'Update branch by rebase' can't rebase a pull request's branch (for example because earlier commits conflict when replayed, even though the current files were reconciled), the page simply reloads: the branch is still out of date, its commits are unchanged, and nothing explains why the update didn't happen. The defect is the missing failure feedback, not that the rebase failed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, turning off a repository’s Issues or Pull Requests unit and later re-enabling it loses that unit’s saved options. Issue tracker restrictions or pull-request merge/deletion choices return to defaults rather than the settings used before the unit was disabled.
logicalBugs.rootCause: handleSettingsPostAdvanced removes disabled RepoUnit records instead of retaining their configuration. When a unit is re-enabled, newRepoUnit builds a fresh record from the defaults rendered in settings. The shared repository-unit lifecycle therefore loses both Issues and Pull Requests configuration.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, turn a repository’s Pull Requests feature off and save, then enable it again. Its merge styles, default merge choice and branch-deletion/manual-merge options return to defaults instead of restoring the choices saved before disabling it.

logicalBugs.description: If the New Pull Request form on a compare page is submitted after a pull request (a proposed code change) for the same head and base branches was opened elsewhere (for example in another tab), Gitea creates a second open pull request for the same branches without any warning. The web create path doesn't check for an existing open pull request, although the compare page normally shows View Pull Request for such a pair and the API refuses duplicates.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The compare GET checks for an existing branch pair, but the web create POST does not revalidate uniqueness at the mutation boundary. Two forms can therefore create the same open head/base pair.
reproductionPaths: If the New Pull Request form on a compare page is submitted after a pull request for the same head and base branches was opened elsewhere (for example in another tab), Gitea creates a second open pull request for the same branches without any warning. The web create path doesn't check for an existing open pull request, although the compare page normally shows View Pull Request for such a pair and the API refuses duplicates.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, immediately after Update branch by rebase, the pull request's +/- totals beside the tabs include changes from the base branch (for example +3 -1 instead of +2 -1). Files Changed shows the correct totals, and the Conversation page corrects itself after navigating away and back.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Candidate timing mechanism: Update defers a goroutine calling AddTestPullRequestTask, and UpdatePullRequest redirects after a fixed one-second sleep. GetPullDiffStats calculates against pull.MergeBase plus the current head ref, so a stale merge-base can include base changes after rebase until the check updates it. The source establishes asynchronous scheduling and the stat inputs, but the report-specific stale merge-base/read interleaving has not been traced. This is a source-informed hypothesis; the exact mechanism has not been confirmed in execution.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, immediately after Update branch by rebase, the pull request's +/- totals beside the tabs include changes from the base branch (for example +3 -1 instead of +2 -1). Files Changed shows the correct totals, and the Conversation page corrects itself after navigating away and back.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a pull request's diff had become empty against its old base and it is then retargeted to a branch where it does add changes, the merge panel keeps saying 'The changes on this branch are already on the target branch. This will be an empty commit.' while Files Changed shows real changes. The empty status from the old base is never cleared when the target changes; merging still works.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ChangeTargetBranch calls testPullRequestBranchMergeable on the existing PR without first replacing its Empty status with Checking. For a successful nonempty three-way merge, checkConflicts sets Empty only when the resulting tree equals the base and otherwise leaves the prior status unchanged. testPullRequestTmpRepoBranchMergeable then returns early whenever pr.Status is still Empty, before its final Mergeable assignment. ChangeTargetBranch only promotes Checking to Mergeable, so the old Empty value is persisted after a nonempty retarget.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a pull request's diff had become empty against its old base and it is then retargeted to a branch where it does add changes, the merge panel keeps saying 'The changes on this branch are already on the target branch. This will be an empty commit.' while Files Changed shows real changes. The empty status from the old base is never cleared when the target changes; merging still works.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea pull request's Files Changed view, an empty inline comment is blocked, but one containing only spaces is accepted. It's saved as a pending review discussion that shows "No description provided.", and Add single comment publishes it to the timeline as a contentless review comment.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The code-comment form checks Required/nonempty rather than trimmed content and CreateCodeComment persists that content. This path does not use SubmitReviewForm.HasEmptyContent’s trim-based review-body validation.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea pull request's Files Changed view, an empty inline comment is blocked, but one containing only spaces is accepted. It's saved as a pending review discussion that shows "No description provided.", and Add single comment publishes it to the timeline as a contentless review comment.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a newly requested reviewer can see a pull request (a proposed code change) in Review requested without a keyword, yet a matching title search hides it on repository or global pull request lists. Removed requests can likewise remain in keyword results; posting an ordinary comment makes the keyword filter catch up.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Request-review mutations emit a notification whose indexer implementation is inherited as a no-op. Requested reviewer IDs are rebuilt only during a later issue reindex such as an ordinary comment.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Pull Requests list, combining a text search with Type → Review requested shows No results, even though a matching pull request requests your review. Requesting a reviewer never refreshes the search index, so the search doesn't know about the request; Review requested without a search works.

On Gitea’s global Pull Requests dashboard, request a user’s review and then use a matching keyword under Review requested as that user. The request is visible without the keyword, but the same pull request is omitted when the matching text search is added.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, when a pull request's changes are already on the target branch, the merge box says it will create an empty commit and still offers squash merging, but Create squash commit fails and the pull request (a proposed code change) stays open. The squash step commits without allowing an empty commit.
logicalBugs.rootCause: doMergeStyleSquash invokes git commit without --allow-empty although the merge UI permits an empty commit. Git rejects the no-change commit; the generic merge server-error path yields only HTTP 500 feedback. The operation failure and opaque feedback share this reproduction trigger.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a pull request's changes are already on the target branch, the merge box says it will create an empty commit and still offers squash merging, but Create squash commit fails and the pull request stays open. The squash step commits without allowing an empty commit.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, for a pull request (a proposed code change) title near the 255-character limit, clicking "Add WIP: prefix" silently cuts the end of the title to make room, and "Remove WIP: prefix" can't restore it. No error or notification tells the user the title was shortened.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The client prepends WIP to the existing title and posts it without a length check. ChangeIssueTitle uses EllipsisDisplayString(...,255), silently replacing the end of the saved title rather than rejecting the oversized edit.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, for a pull request title near the 255-character limit, clicking "Add WIP: prefix" silently cuts the end of the title to make room, and "Remove WIP: prefix" can't restore it. No error or notification tells the user the title was shortened.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a file with inline review comments is moved into a folder or renamed in a later commit, its comment threads (resolved or pending) no longer appear in the pull request's Files Changed view, even with Show outdated comments enabled. The comments are still tied to the old path.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Code comments are associated with their stored TreePath and the diff/comment loading path does not remap that path through later Git renames. Threads remain attached to the old path even when outdated comments are shown.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a file with inline review comments is moved into a folder or renamed in a later commit, its comment threads (resolved or pending) no longer appear in the pull request's Files Changed view, even with Show outdated comments enabled. The comments are still tied to the old path.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if commits are pushed to a pull request's target branch while the pull request is closed, reopening it doesn't show that the branch is behind or offer the Update branch button, even after a reload. How far behind it is only gets recalculated for open pull requests (proposed code changes) when the target changes.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Push-triggered PR checks select only open unmerged PRs; target advances while closed do not update CommitsBehind. Reopen invokes the conflict-check workflow without the same divergence update, so branch-update controls use stale zero-behind state.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if commits are pushed to a pull request's target branch while the pull request is closed, reopening it doesn't show that the branch is behind or offer the Update branch button, even after a reload. How far behind it is only gets recalculated for open pull requests when the target changes.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on global or organization Issues and Pull Requests, selecting an Author or Assignee and then clicking Open, Closed or an ownership sidebar link drops that user filter. Results and counts broaden to records excluded by the previously selected author/assignee, including when the ownership link was already active.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dashboard builds $queryLink without poster or assignee, then uses it for ownership and Open/Closed links. $queryLinkWithFilter contains those fields but is only used by the filter and sort controls. Global and organization dashboards share this template.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea organization's Pull Requests page, switching between Open and Closed while an Author or Assignee filter is selected drops those filters, so pull requests by other authors or with other assignees appear.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, set or change an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request’s due date in its sidebar, then search for matching text and sort by Nearest or Farthest due date. Global searches, and the repository issue-search path, can display the new dates but order results using earlier dates or as if no date were set. Posting an ordinary comment on the affected work item makes the search order catch up.
logicalBugs.rootCause: UpdateIssueDeadline updates the database and timeline only; indexerNotifier has no due-date change hook. Keyword searches sort the indexed DeadlineUnix from the last indexing job until another supported notification reindexes the issue.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, change a pull request’s due date from its sidebar, then use a matching text search and due-date sorting on the global Pull Requests dashboard. The row shows the new date while its position still reflects the previous saved date, instead of updating the search order.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea pull request’s Files Changed view, conversation navigation is meant to take the user to an inline discussion. If the discussion belongs to a collapsed file, navigation changes the comment destination but does not expand that file, leaving the requested conversation hidden.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Previous/Next changes only the location hash. The hashchange path scrolls without unfolding; the initial page-load path explicitly unfolds target files, explaining why reload works.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea pull request’s Files Changed view, conversation navigation is meant to take the user to an inline discussion. If the discussion belongs to a collapsed file, navigation changes the comment destination but does not expand that file, leaving the requested conversation hidden.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, Quote Reply on an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) inserts nonempty quoted text into the comment composer, but Comment stays disabled and switching to Preview/Write does not enable it. Typing an ordinary character can make the same composer submittable.
logicalBugs.rootCause: tryOnQuoteReply uses ComboMarkdownEditor.value(v). The textarea setter changes value without dispatching EventEditorContentChanged, while comment button state listens to that event and upload events. Typing finally resynchronizes it.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, choosing Quote Reply populates the comment composer, but Comment stays disabled. Switching to Preview and back to Write does not enable posting the generated quote.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, compare commits can call different branches equal when the selected head is an ancestor of the base. Reversing the comparison shows commits and a file diff, but the ancestor-to-descendant direction shows the equal-branches/empty-comparison message despite different trees.
logicalBugs.rootCause: PrepareCompareDiff sets IsNothingToCompare when headCommitID equals the comparison MergeBase. This uses the empty base-to-head commit range from merge-base semantics as an equality test, although the selected branch trees can differ. Repository comparison and pull-request comparison share this decision.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, when a fork's branch has changes and the comparison is reversed (the fork branch as base and the upstream branch as head, for example via Switch head and base and Switch comparison type), the compare page shows "These branches are equal" and no files, although the branches' contents differ. It happens whenever the head is an ancestor of the base.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, if a pull request (a proposed code change) is closed in another tab while its merge confirmation is open, submitting the merge is correctly refused with "The pull request has been closed.", but the page doesn't update: it keeps the green Open badge and an enabled merge button until it's reloaded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The merge request error path displays the returned error without refreshing the issue state or merge availability. A correctly rejected already-closed PR therefore retains its previous page badge and controls.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if a pull request is closed in another tab while its merge confirmation is open, submitting the merge is correctly refused with "The pull request has been closed.", but the page doesn't update: it keeps the green Open badge and an enabled merge button until it's reloaded.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after choosing Type > Assigned to you, switching back to All issues (tracked work items) or to another ownership type can retain the old implicit assignee restriction. Repository/milestone (a named group of work items) issue lists and organization pull request (a proposed code change) lists then omit otherwise matching records despite showing the new Type selection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The issue handler exports the effective self assignee after Type=assigned; shared filter_list copies that AssigneeID into subsequent Type links. Created by you therefore retains an unintended assignment restriction.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after selecting Assigned to you, switching Type to Created by you shows No results instead of the user's unassigned pull request. The prior assignment restriction remains in effect.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, deleting an issue (a tracked work item) or pull request (a proposed code change) discussion comment removes its timeline card immediately, but the issue comment total or pull request Conversation badge keeps the previous count. Reload is needed for the header count to agree with the remaining comments.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The delete handler removes the timeline DOM node and updates review counters, but never changes the issue header count, leaving the original server-rendered value until navigation.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, deleting a pull request discussion comment removes it from the timeline but leaves the Conversation badge unchanged until reload.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after approving another author’s pull request (a proposed code change), Reviewed by you can list it without a query but hide it under a matching title keyword on global or organization Pull Requests. Posting an ordinary comment makes the keyword search find the same persisted review.
logicalBugs.rootCause: SubmitReview emits PullRequestReview; indexerNotifier inherits its empty implementation. ReviewedIDs are rebuilt only on later reindex, so indexed keyword searches miss persisted approvals.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, approve another author’s pull request, then use Reviewed by you on the global Pull Requests dashboard with a matching title keyword. The persisted review is listed without a keyword but omitted from the matching keyword results until another indexing action occurs.

In Gitea, after reviewing another author’s pull request, search its matching title under Reviewed by you on an organization’s Pull Requests dashboard. The review exists, but the pull request disappears only when the matching keyword is combined with that review filter.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a team can be asked to review a pull request (a proposed code change) on behalf of its members. On an organization’s Pull Requests list, the requested pull request appears under Review requested without a keyword but disappears when a matching title keyword is added. A direct request to the individual user can be found, while posting an ordinary comment does not repair the team-only request, distinguishing this from a temporarily stale individual-review search.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Issue index conversion adds Review.ReviewerID for requested reviews, without expanding ReviewerTeamID membership. A viewer’s team-only request therefore cannot match their user ID even after reindexing.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea organization’s Pull Requests dashboard, use a matching keyword under Review requested for a pull request that requests review from a team you belong to. The matching pull request is omitted instead of treating the team’s request as a request for its members.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after a pull request's source branch is deleted (for example by merging with Delete branch), the pull request's own page shows the branch name as plain text, but every pull request (a proposed code change) list (repository, global, organization, milestone (a named group of work items) and subscription lists) still shows it as a link, which opens a Page Not Found error. The list template always links the branch without checking whether it still exists.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared issue-list PR branch markup constructs /src/branch/HeadBranch without the branch-existence guard used by the PR detail page. Deleted heads remain actionable links to 404 across list surfaces.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, after a pull request’s source branch is deleted, its own detail page shows the branch as plain text, but repository, global, organization, milestone and subscription lists keep a clickable branch link. Following that link opens Page Not Found instead of making the deleted branch visibly unavailable.
